title: Globalizing synchronized local ordinary blowup towers
statement:
Let $X$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $S$ a finite set of pairwise incomparable points with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,s}=r\ge1$ for every $s\in S$, and $p:P\to X$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $P$ reduced Noetherian [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Noetherian means having a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings; dimension is the supremum of lengths of prime chains. Put $P_s=P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,s}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose on $\coprod_{s\in S}P_s$ a finite ordered tower of ordinary blowups with coherent reduced nowhere dense centers is given [def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent], and each center is supported over the closed points of these local bases. Nowhere dense means that its underlying closed subset contains no nonempty open subset. Empty centers on individual components are allowed.

There is a canonical tower on $P$: at each stage its center is the schematic closure of the union of the corresponding local centers in the current ambient scheme, meaning the smallest closed subscheme through which those centers map [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Its restriction to every $P_s$ is the given tower, with its empty stages; it is independent of auxiliary open neighbourhoods used to spread the local centers. Every nonempty global center is reduced, nowhere dense, and its image in $X$ is a union of closures of members of $S$, with pure codimension $r$ (every generic point of the image has local-ring dimension $r$). The inverse image of the generic points of this image is schematically dense in the center: functions are determined by their restrictions to the corresponding local schemes. If $P=W$ is a closed subscheme of a Noetherian ambient $X$-scheme $M$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the same closure centers may instead be blown up in $M$; the resulting strict transform of $W$ restricts over each $s$ to its given iterated blowup [def-nagata-strict-transform].

For a flat base change $f:X'\to X$ between Noetherian schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], taking the schematic images of the full pulled-back local centers, on $P_s\times_X X'$, gives exactly the scheme-theoretic pullback of the global tower, including its center ideals. The same holds for the ambient construction. No reduction of a pulled-back ideal is made. If instead the tower, or its ambient construction in $M\times_XX'$, is reconstructed from the local schemes at the finite set $S'$ of generic points of $f^{-1}(\bigcup_{s\in S}\overline{\{s\}})$, it agrees with that pullback provided the inverse image of $S'$ is schematically dense in every pulled-back global center. It suffices for this extra condition that all those pulled-back centers are reduced. In either comparison, only empty centers may be contracted. General flat pullback alone does not assert reducedness or preservation of the integer $r$.

source.place: §2.2.7 (pushforward by schematic closure), Lemma 2.1.2, §4.2.1 and Lemmas 4.2.4--4.2.5, printed pp.7,10--11,28--29; simultaneous centers rather than separately ordered local towers; Temkin arXiv:0904.1592v2, read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this combined assertion.

proof.text: We construct the tower by induction on its given finite length $N$, retaining all stages. Write $T=P_i$ and $D_s\subset T_s=T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,s}$ for the next given center, using the inductively supplied identification with the local tower. At $i=0$ this identification is the definition of $P_s$. The canonical map $T_s\to T$ is a monomorphism: on a base affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $s$ it is localization by $A\setminus\mathfrak p_s$, and a map into this localization has at most one lift because all these denominators must be units. It is flat by localization-flatness and stability under base change. All $T_s$ and $D_s$ are Noetherian: on each of the finitely many affine charts of $T$, localization preserves finite generation of ideals (an ideal is the extension of its contraction); quotients do also. Consequently $D=\coprod_sD_s$ is Noetherian. The map $D\to T$ is quasi-compact, since the inverse image of an affine open is an open subset of a Noetherian space.

Let $C=\operatorname{SIm}(D\to T)$. The quasi-compact image theorem makes this a closed subscheme defined by the kernel of restriction of functions to $D$, with injective restriction from $\mathcal O_C$ to the pushforward of $\mathcal O_D$. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ its ideal $I$ is finitely generated because $B$ is Noetherian. Kernels of maps from finite free $B$-modules to $I$ are submodules of finite free Noetherian modules and hence finitely generated. Thus this quasi-coherent ideal is coherent in the stated sense. Since $D$ is reduced, the reduced-image theorem identifies $C$ with the reduced induced structure on $\overline{D}$. In particular it is reduced, and it is empty exactly when every $D_s$ is empty.

For $t\in S$, apply flat base change of schematic images to $D\to T$ and $T_t\to T$. The $s=t$ summand of $D\times_TT_t$ is $D_t$, since $T_t\to T$ is a monomorphism. Every other summand is empty. Indeed a point in the $s$ summand maps to $s\in X$, whereas every point of $T_t$ maps to a generalization of $t$; this would say that $s$ generalizes $t$, contrary to incomparability. A scheme with empty underlying space is empty. Hence $C\times_TT_t$ is the schematic image of the closed immersion $D_t\hookrightarrow T_t$, namely $D_t$, with its full scheme structure.

Define $P_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_C(T)$. Flat base change for ordinary blowups and the preceding equality identify its restriction to each local base with the prescribed blowup in $D_s$, including the empty-center identity stage. The reduced-Noetherian blowup lemma preserves the induction's hypothesis on $T$. Each blowup is proper because its coherent ideal is of finite type, and proper composition shows that every $P_i\to X$ is proper. Repeat this induction for $i=0,\ldots,N-1$. It terminates after exactly $N$ stages.

Here is the support calculation at one induction stage. By finiteness of Noetherian components and scheme sobriety, write each $D_s$ as a finite union of irreducible components with generic points $d_{sj}$. Each $d_{sj}$ maps to $s$. Its image in $T$ has irreducible closure $E_{sj}$; its own point is the generic point of that closure, because continuous maps preserve the specialization relation. The underlying set of $C$ is the finite union of these $E_{sj}$. Thus every irreducible component $E$ of $C$ equals one of the maximal $E_{sj}$, and its generic point maps to a member of $S$. Conversely each nonempty $D_s$ contributes points over $s$.

The image of $C$ in $X$ is closed, since $P_i\to X$ is proper and $C$ is closed in $P_i$. It is contained in $\bigcup_{D_s\ne\varnothing}\overline{\{s\}}$: that closed inverse image already contains $D$ and hence its closure. It contains each such $s$, hence also its closure. This proves equality. Incomparability makes precisely these $s$ its component-generic points, so its pure codimension is $r$ by hypothesis. The map from the disjoint union of the restrictions of $C$ to their local bases has schematic image $C$, because it is exactly $D\to C$, whose restriction on functions is injective by the image-kernel theorem. This is the required schematic density, and includes the assertion that a local function vanishing on all those local restrictions vanishes.

To check nowhere-density, suppose $C$ contained a nonempty open of $T$. By the component cover and sobriety, that open contains a generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component $F$ of $T$. Since $C$ is closed, $F\subset C$, and maximality of $F$ makes it an irreducible component of $C$. Step 5 gives $p_i(\eta)=s\in S$. Localizing the base at $s$ preserves this generic point and its local ring: every inverted base function is already a unit there. The preimage of $F$ is a component of $T_s$ and is contained in $D_s=C\times_TT_s$. A Noetherian scheme has finitely many components; removing its other components leaves a nonempty open subset of this component. Thus $D_s$ contains a nonempty open of $T_s$, a contradiction. Hence $C$ is nowhere dense.

The kernel description also proves canonicity and independence. A center obtained as the schematic closure of the given $D_s$ must have ideal $\ker(\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_D)$ and therefore equals $C$. Applying this observation at each stage identifies the next blowup and then its prescribed local centers. In particular spreading on auxiliary neighborhoods, followed by taking closures, gives this same tower whenever it gives the prescribed local centers schematically densely. There is no uniqueness assertion for extensions with additional components supported away from the specified local bases.

For the ambient assertion induct on the same stage index. Initially $W=P$ is closed in $M$. If its current strict transform is identified with $P_i$, the maps of the $D_s$ into the ambient scheme factor through that closed subscheme. Their schematic image in the ambient scheme is exactly $C$ with its composite closed immersion: on affine rings the kernel of $A\to B\to\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ is the inverse image of the kernel in $B$, where $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ defines $P_i$. Thus the ambient center restricts to precisely $C$ on $P_i$. The strict-transform-is-blowup theorem now identifies the next strict transform with $\operatorname{Bl}_C(P_i)=P_{i+1}$, as a closed subscheme of the next ambient blowup and compatibly with its projection. This proves the assertion for the entire finite tower.

proof.text: Let $X'\to X$ be flat. At a stage already identified with the pullback of $P_i$, the map $P_i\times_XX'\to P_i$ is flat. Flat base change of schematic images says that the image of the full $D\times_XX'$ is $C\times_XX'$, with ideal $I_C\mathcal O_{P_i\times_XX'}$. Flat base change of blowups identifies the next stage. Induction proves the assertion for the whole tower. The argument does not replace $D\times_XX'$ by its reduction or by restrictions to selected generic points. Applied to the ambient centers it proves the same identity there; strict-transform-is-blowup then gives the comparison on $W$. Empty centers give identity stages and may be deleted in their existing order.

If one reconstructs from the new local bases at $S'$, the stated schematic-density hypothesis says precisely that the image of the union of the restricted center maps into $C'=C\times_XX'$ is all of $C'$. Composing with its closed immersion into $P_i\times_XX'$ gives schematic image $C'$ again: the kernels of restriction to these local centers and to $C'$ coincide. Therefore the newly reconstructed center is $C'$ at every stage. Induction using flat blowup base change gives the desired comparison, retaining all nonempty ideals. For the ambient construction, with $M_i$ the $i$-th ambient blowup of Step 9, the local centers map into $M_i\times_XX'$ through the closed subscheme $P_i\times_XX'$, so by the kernel computation of Step 9 their schematic image there is $C'$ with its composite closed immersion; strict-transform-is-blowup then identifies the next strict transform of $W\times_XX'$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{C'}(P_i\times_XX')$, and induction gives the ambient comparison.

Finally assume every $C'=C\times_XX'$ is reduced. Let $Z\subset X$ be the reduced image of $C\to X$. Step 5 shows $C\to Z$ is maximally dominant: all component-generic points go to the generic points of $Z$, which are the active members of $S$. The flat-maximal-dominance lemma applied to $Z'=Z\times_XX'\to Z$ shows that every generic point of $C'$ maps to a generic point of $Z'$. These belong to $S'$: flat maximal dominance also makes their images in $Z$ generic, so they map to an active $s$; such a point cannot lie in the inverse image of an inactive point closure, by incomparability. Thus active components remain components in the full union. The finite union of restrictions of $C'$ to the local bases at $S'$ thus has topologically dense image in $C'$. Its source is Noetherian, so this morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Reducedness of $C'$ and the reduced-dense-image theorem promote topological density to schematic density. This proves the stated sufficient condition without claiming reducedness under arbitrary flat pullback.
